##### Summary
Closes #7738 

##### Component Name
ACLK

##### Description of testing that the developer performed
Extensive testing has been performed during the smoke-test sessions, and then again locally. The review should not try to test this PR - setting up the test-configuration is not a good investment of time when it was done in smoke-testing, this will be tested again extensively on the real test system.

##### Additional Information
Please perform the highest-quality review that you can within a limited amount of time (2-3 hours?). There is a list of known issues in the ACLK that this PR does not fix (#8279). Because functional correctness is being handled via separate testing please focus on code quality / safety.

issue_context.title: Fix outstanding issues on the ACLK implementation
issue_context.body:
#### Summary

This is a list of outstanding implementation issues for tracking.
comments:
Things that have not been converted to issues yet (depends on whether they are fixed as part of ongoing work or handled separately):
- [ ] Broker kicks the agent out after 30 seconds - missing heartbeat?
- [ ] Memory leaks, e.g. https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/8167#issuecomment-590064204
- [x] The uninitialised variables inside the JSON parser that valgrind is complaining about.
- [x] On a reconnect `mqtt_init` is called again and causes a memory-leak.
- [ ] The LWS event-loop returns instantly in the time after initialization, but before connection. This floods the library with calls and breaks something. A 100ms delay has been added as a work-around but must be fixed properly before we do load-testing.
- [x] All queries are ignored during pop-corning, but commands from the cloud are in the same queue for processing so the agent would ignore requests during this period.
- [x] Any query resets the pop-corning timer (including encapsulated queries) so pop-corning can go on indefinitely.
- [x] The implementation of the time-out / check is wrong and it will always sleep 10s longer than necessary.
- [x] The `smoke-test` branch seems to stop randomly on Ubuntu / Debian systems. Investigate.
- [x] The behavior depends on which json parser is in use. If the JSONC external dependency is available then it works, it seems to break on the internal version.
- [x] The `msg-id` fields for messages originating at the agent need to be randomized uuids.
This issue has been inactive for 30 days. It will be closed in one week, unless it is updated.
There is nothing left in this epic - I reassigned the documentation issue to the cloud blockers epic.

review_comments: I am not sure we should log every callback even as LWS library grows callbacks can be added that we are simply not interested in. But up to you

That is a fair point. My reasoning is as follows: we need to be sure about every callback that is generated by an external dependency. In a sense this part of the code is there to enforce white-listing of those events, i.e. one of us has sat and read the docs and made an explicit effort to put it onto the "don't care" list. If the library changes in the future and new callbacks are generated then somebody needs to perform that explicit step and this logging will force that to happen.
